issues.title: Unjustified classical differentiation at the Sobolev endpoint

failure_location.quote: combined with the smoothness of the activation function $\sigma$ and the windows $\varphi$ and  $\phi$, allows us to differentiate $\tilde{\rho}$ with respect to the $x$-variable up to the order $n$

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem permits k=n. A W^{n,infinity} activation need not possess a classical nth derivative, yet the old proof justifies differentiation by the activation's alleged smoothness and bounds the result by a C^{|alpha|} norm, followed by an undefined W^{m,infinity} norm. The old ramp lemma supplies a concrete endpoint example in W^{1,infinity} that has kink points and is not C^1. Hence the classical calculation is not justified as written. Weak derivatives do suffice, but that argument was absent in version 1.
issues.overall_effect: The uniform W^{n,r} bound for the weighted local dictionary is not established at k=n, blocking the application of the type-2 approximation proposition and therefore the local theorem and its listed consequences.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the classical differentiation passage by a weak-derivative calculation. For every multi-index of order at most n, apply the affine Sobolev chain rule and weak Leibniz rule, using the weak derivatives of σ in L-infinity through order n, and reproduce the same uniform weighted W^{n,r} bound for the atoms. The variation-space and Maurey arguments then apply unchanged, preserving the theorem and all four listed consequences with their original hypotheses, conclusions, and N^{-1/2} rate.
issues.why_classification: The endpoint calculation is genuinely unjustified and therefore is not a typo, as the ramp example demonstrates. Nevertheless, affine composition and multiplication by smooth windows in W^{n,infinity} require only a short, standard weak-derivative argument. That local repair preserves the dictionary, uniform bound, approximation rate, and every listed dependent result without a new construction or substantive weakening.

new_version_repair_locator.quote: the function $\tilde{\rho}$ admits weak derivatives with respect to $x$ up to order $n$, provided that $n\le k$

issues.title: Lost complex phase in the local representing measure
issues.failure_explanation: Let A=(V_phi sigma)(t,tau). Equation eq:phase_identity requires the factor A^{-1}. With the old definition C=|A|^{-1}, the asserted integral equals (A/|A|)f rather than f. The hypotheses do not force A/|A|=1: for the admissible choice sigma=1, varphi(s)=exp(-pi s^2), t=1/4 and tau=1, one obtains A=-i exp(-pi). Thus the old representing measure does not give the identity asserted in the proof.
issues.overall_effect: The old proof does not establish the exact representation of f used to place it in the local variation space, so the local approximation theorem and its four listed consequences remain unestablished until the phase is restored.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Let A=(V_φσ)(t,τ) and use A^{-1}, rather than |A|^{-1}, as the coefficient in the exact representation and representing measure. Use |A|^{-1} only when taking total variations and estimating constants. Carrying this corrected coefficient through the local theorem restores all four listed consequences without changing any statement or bound.
issues.why_classification: The old phase identity and the immediately preceding substitution already display the uniquely required coefficient A^{-1}. The later modulus is therefore a transcriptional loss of phase, not a choice requiring new mathematics. Restoring the forced complex inverse makes the representation exact, while all norm estimates continue to depend only on |A|^{-1}.

issues.title: False global lower bound for the ReLU STFT
issues.failure_explanation: The corollary quantifies over every (x,omega). At (0,0), lem:relu-origin gives |V_phi sigma(0,0)|=1/(2pi), exactly equal to the right-hand side of eq:lowerbound, contradicting the strict inequality. Moreover, for x<0 and omega=0, the explicit formula has a negative first term while the defining integral is positive, so even replacing > by >= does not restore the bound. At x=0, integration by parts in the defining Fourier integral gives decay as |omega| tends to infinity, whereas the proposed right-hand side remains 1/(2pi). The proof's triangle inequality establishes only |V| >= T_2-|T_1|, not |V|>T_2.
issues.overall_effect: The quantitative lower-bound clause of cor:31 is false and cannot serve as a proof of non-vanishing. No later formal result depends on this bound; the corollary's separate non-vanishing defect is represented by C06.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Withdraw the global quantitative lower-bound clause and its invalid triangle-inequality argument, while retaining the separately proved explicit STFT formula and value at the origin. No non-vanishing conclusion should be inferred from this bound. A replacement would require a genuinely proved, recognizably comparable global lower estimate; none is established by either source.
issues.why_classification: The claim fails not merely at a strict-versus-weak boundary: it has equality at the origin, fails in other finite regimes, and contradicts the STFT's decay in frequency at x=0. Thus no local inequality edit repairs it. The only established complete resolution removes the all-point quantitative guarantee, and no comparable lower bound survives. That is major mathematical loss even though no later formal result depends on the clause.

issues.title: Invalid proof of universal ReLU-STFT non-vanishing

failure_location.quote: If it vanished at any real point $(x_0,\omega_0)$, then by the identity theorem for analytic functions it would vanish on a non-empty open set

issues.failure_explanation: The proof invokes the identity theorem after assuming only one real zero. No premise establishes a set of zeros with an accumulation interior or an open zero set. The claimed inference is refuted by elementary analytic examples such as z mapped to z, which has a zero without vanishing on an open set. Lemma lem:relu-origin supplies one nonzero value and hence proves only that this STFT is not identically zero; it does not exclude other zeros.
issues.overall_effect: The universal non-vanishing conclusion of cor:31 is unsupported, and the old experimental discussion overstates what is needed for Condition (A). No later formal result depends on universality: continuity together with a nonzero origin value suffices to choose nearby t and nonzero tau.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the universal zero-free claim and the invalid identity-theorem proof by the contained valid statement obtained from V_φσ(x,ω)=e^{-πx²}H(x-iω), where H(z)=∫_0^∞ t exp(-πt²+2πtz) dt. The function H is entire and H(0)=1/(2π), so its zero set is at most discrete; consequently the ReLU STFT is nonzero outside at most a discrete subset of the phase plane. Continuity at the origin then supplies nearby t and nonzero τ satisfying Condition (A).
issues.why_classification: A single zero of a nonconstant analytic function cannot be excluded by the identity theorem, so the old proof does not establish universal non-vanishing. The one-variable entire-function factorization gives a contained replacement argument and a recognizably comparable global statement—non-vanishing apart from at most isolated points—while preserving the only needed application, Condition (A). The repair exceeds minor severity because it requires a replacement argument and relinquishes the central all-points guarantee, but it avoids both global reconstruction and major regime loss.
